In the Deferred Acceptance algorithm, my goal is to maximize my chances of getting into the best possible school given my preferences and priorities.

My true preference order is y > x > w > z, which means I most want y, then x, then w, and z is my least preferred.

My priority ranks are critical: 
- At x, I have top priority (1)
- At z, I also have top priority (1)
- At w and y, I have lower priority (2)

The top priority at x and z, combined with my preference for y and x, suggests I should rank y first (my top preference), then x (where I have top priority), then w, and z last.

By putting y first, I signal my strongest desire. By putting x second, I leverage my top priority there. Ranking w third keeps an option open, and z last reflects its low appeal.

This strategy balances my true preferences with my strategic positioning in the matching process.
